text:
maya: Quick heads-up — perf bump on a subset of SM103 machines when sequence length > 256. Seen across two farms, looks like fallback to generic matmul path.
jason: which kernel path is doing the fallback? fallback to `matmul_ref` or something custom?
maya: seems to be falling back to `matmul_tc_bf16_sm103` not being selected; runtime picks `matmul_tc_bf16_autotile` normally but here it chooses `matmul_ref->softmax_generic` chain. repro on perf-prod-4 and perf-prod-7.
priya: pasting a short profiler snapshot from perf-prod-4 run (seq_len=320, batch=8):
```
[probe] device 0: NVIDIA SM103 GPU
probe: driver=550.12 cuda=12.1 pciid=0000:1b:00.0
capflags: sm=103 tensor_cores=1 bf16=1 fp8=0
runtime: selected_kernel = matmul_ref (est 1.35ms)
autotune-scores: matmul_tc_bf16_autotile=0.86 matmul_ref=1.35
heuristics: seq_threshold_fastpath=256 hysteresis=64 batching=auto
kvcache: hit_rate=0.73 evictions=11/min
```
priya: note: autotune score for `matmul_tc_bf16_autotile` looks fine but selection logic ignored it because `capflag.tensor_cores` was momentarily 0 on probe start (race with driver init?).
leo: any evidence of driver returning inconsistent flags? we've seen 537 weirdness before.
priya: yes — device probe logs show a transient "tensor_core: disabled during SM init" earlier in boot logs. snippet:
```
[boot] sm_init: detected sm=103
[boot] tensor_core: temp-disable until firmware ready
[probe] capflags tensor_cores=0 (cached)
[probe] after 300ms, kernel list recomputed but selection used cached capflags
```
jason: aha — selection is using cached capflags at runtime startup and never re-evaluates once kernels are cached. So when the capability flips on shortly after, we still use the conservative kernel.
maya: that matches the perf delta: at seq_len=320 matmul_tc_bf16_autotile is ~0.86ms vs matmul_ref 1.35ms => ~36% slower path being used for minutes until process restart.
priya: quick mitigation: add a probe-refresh window or re-evaluate kernel selection on the first eviction/miss event. Proposed patch: on first 60s after startup if `capflags.tensor_cores==0` and subsequent probe shows 1, force `rebuild_kernel_cache()` for that device only.
leo: small patch, low risk. Could also add hysteresis tweak: increase seq_threshold_fastpath from 256->320 for SM103 so fewer borderline fallbacks, but that's masking root cause.
jason: also noticed KV cache behavior: when kernel switched, KV cache eviction spiked ~3x because the ref kernel uses different KV layout flags. We need to ensure KV cache compatibility or avoid switching mid-run.
priya: profiler excerpt showing KV thrash during fallback window (seq_len 320, burst workload):
```
kvcache: layout=compact_v2 kernel_hint=autotile -> switch -> layout=legacy_v1
kv_evictions/sec: 4.2 -> 12.9
latency p95 tokens: 12.8ms -> 21.6ms
```
maya: that explains customer-reported latency spikes yesterday on dedicated nodes.
jason: plan: 1) immediate hotfix: rebuild kernel cache when capflags flip within first 60s (pr to eng-runtime-hotfix), 2) add an instrumentation flag to detect cached capflags mismatch and log a high-severity metric, 3) follow-up: make kernel cache key include `probe_epoch` so it auto-invalidates on capability change.
priya: I'll open the PR with small patch and unit tests for `device_probe()` path. Also adding a microbench job in CI that simulates delayed tensor-core enablement.
leo: can you add a perf-run to perf-ci? runtime-bot: @perf-ci run microbench:sm103-delay (seqs: 64, 256, 320, 512) using perf-prod-4
runtime-bot: Scheduled run https://perf.internal/runs/4598761234-01 (ETA ~15m)
maya: thanks. one more note: let's adjust the selection code to prefer `matmul_tc_bf16_autotile` for seq >= 192 on SM103 as a safe bias — should reduce regression risk until probe fix lands.
jason: agree. We'll avoid changing global thresholds — make it per-arch table entry.
priya: PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/7841 — includes patch + tests + kv layout guard that prevents mid-run kv layout switches (falls back to logging + reject)
maya: cool. after runtime-bot completes perf run let's validate numbers and ship to staging then dedicated hosts.
runtime-bot: perf-run completed. summary:
```
seq=64: no change
seq=256: matmul_tc path selected in 92% hosts, median 0.95ms -> baseline 0.98ms
seq=320: before patch median 1.44ms, after patch median 0.89ms
seq=512: still uses ref on 30% hosts due to fp8 disabled; median 2.8ms -> 2.82ms
kv_evictions: reduced to baseline after kernel-cache-rebuild
```
leo: numbers look good. Please get hotfix merged and roll to staging.
maya: filing a quick incident note and will notify support templates for impacted customers. thanks team :thumbsup:
